title: The Taxi Drivers’ Brains
subtitle: 倫敦計程車司機的大腦
source: 原創教學文章；研究內容依 Maguire et al.（2000）PNAS 原始論文，2026-10-21 核對

sources.title: Maguire, E. A., et al. (2000). Navigation-related structural change in the hippocampi of taxi drivers. PNAS, 97(8), 4398–4403.

beginner.title: A Map Inside the Head
paras: London is a very old city with thousands of streets. Many of them are small, crooked and confusing. To drive one of London’s famous black taxis, drivers must pass a very difficult test called The Knowledge. They have to learn the city’s streets so well that they can find the best route without a map.
倫敦是一座非常古老的城市，有成千上萬條街道，很多又小又彎、讓人搞不清楚方向。想開倫敦著名的黑色計程車，司機必須通過一項非常困難的考試，叫做「The Knowledge（倫敦知識）」。他們要把城市的街道記得滾瓜爛熟，不看地圖也能找到最好的路線。

Learning all these streets takes a long time. In one study, the drivers had spent about two years, on average, training for The Knowledge. For some drivers in the study, the training took less than a year; for others, it took three and a half years. Scientist Eleanor Maguire wondered: does all this learning change the brain?
要學會這些街道得花很長的時間。在一項研究中，司機們平均花了大約兩年準備這項考試。在這項研究裡，有些司機的訓練不到一年，有些則花了三年半。科學家艾莉諾．馬奎爾好奇：這麼多的學習，會改變大腦嗎？

In 2000, she and her team used brain scans to study 16 London taxi drivers. They compared them with men who did not drive taxis. They looked closely at a part of the brain called the hippocampus, which helps us remember places and find our way.
2000 年，她和團隊用腦部掃描研究了 16 位倫敦計程車司機，並把他們和不開計程車的男性做比較。他們仔細觀察了大腦裡一個叫做海馬迴的部位，它幫助我們記住地點、找到方向。

The back part of the hippocampus was larger in the taxi drivers. Also, drivers who had worked longer tended to have a larger back part. This suggests that the brain may change as we use it. The scientists called this “plasticity”. In other words, the more the drivers used their memory for places, the more this part of the brain seemed to grow.
計程車司機海馬迴的後側比較大。而且，開車年資越久的司機，後側往往越大。這表示大腦可能會隨著我們的使用而改變。科學家稱之為「可塑性」。換句話說，司機越常使用對地點的記憶，大腦的這個部位似乎就長得越大。

Today, most of us use phone maps. They are fast and helpful. But this study makes us think: if we never find our way by ourselves, what happens to the map inside our heads? Scientists are still studying that question. Maybe sometimes it is worth putting the phone away and exploring.
現在，我們大多數人都用手機地圖，又快又方便。但這項研究讓我們思考：如果我們從來不靠自己找路，腦中的那張地圖會怎麼樣？科學家仍在研究這個問題。也許有時候，值得把手機收起來，自己探索看看。

intermediate.title: The Taxi Drivers’ Brains
paras: To earn a licence to drive a black cab in London, drivers must pass one of the most demanding tests in the world, known simply as The Knowledge. They must memorise the layout of a huge and irregular city — its streets, landmarks and best routes — and then prove they can plan journeys from memory. For scientists interested in learning, these drivers offered a rare opportunity.
想取得倫敦黑色計程車的駕駛執照，司機必須通過世界上最嚴苛的考試之一，簡稱「The Knowledge」。他們得記住一座巨大又不規則的城市的布局——街道、地標和最佳路線——並證明自己能憑記憶規劃行程。對研究學習的科學家來說，這些司機提供了一個難得的機會。

Neuroscientist Eleanor Maguire and her colleagues wanted to know whether this kind of intensive learning could change the physical structure of the adult brain. In a study published in 2000, they scanned the brains of 16 licensed London taxi drivers, who had spent an average of about two years training for The Knowledge, and compared them with men who did not drive taxis. All of the drivers had been licensed for more than a year and a half, and some had been driving for decades.
神經科學家艾莉諾．馬奎爾和同事想知道，這種密集的學習，是否能改變成人大腦的實體結構。在 2000 年發表的研究中，他們掃描了 16 位持照倫敦計程車司機的大腦——這些司機平均花了約兩年準備考試——並與不開計程車的男性比較。所有司機都已持照超過一年半，有些人已經開了幾十年的車。

The researchers focused on the hippocampus, a region known to be important for spatial memory and navigation. They found that the posterior, or rear, part of the hippocampus was significantly larger in the taxi drivers, while a front region was larger in the comparison group. In other words, the drivers’ brains showed a different distribution of tissue, not simply more of it.
研究者聚焦於海馬迴——一個已知對空間記憶與導航很重要的區域。他們發現，計程車司機海馬迴的後側明顯較大，而前側的某個區域則是對照組較大。換句話說，司機的大腦呈現的是組織分布的不同，而不只是「比較多」。

A natural objection is that people with larger hippocampi might simply be more likely to become taxi drivers. To test this, the team looked at how long each person had worked as a driver. The longer someone had spent on the job, the larger the right posterior hippocampus tended to be. This suggested that the difference was acquired through experience rather than present from birth. It did not prove the point beyond doubt, but it made a strong case.
一個很自然的質疑是：也許海馬迴本來就比較大的人，比較可能去當計程車司機。為了檢驗這一點，團隊觀察了每個人當司機的時間長短。結果發現，工作年資越長，右側海馬迴後側往往越大。這表示差異是透過經驗後天形成的，而不是天生就有。這並沒有毫無疑問地證明這一點，但已是相當有力的論證。

The study became famous because it showed that the adult brain is more changeable than many people once believed. It also raises a modern question. If finding our way builds the brain’s internal map, what happens when we let phone apps do the navigating? Researchers are still investigating, but the taxi drivers remind us that the brain tends to grow in the directions we exercise it.
這項研究之所以出名，是因為它顯示成人的大腦比許多人過去以為的更具可塑性。它也引出一個現代的問題：如果自己找路能建構大腦裡的地圖，那麼當我們讓手機應用程式替我們導航時，會發生什麼事？研究者仍在探討，但這些計程車司機提醒我們：大腦往往朝著我們鍛鍊它的方向成長。

advanced.title: How Learning Shapes the Brain
paras: For much of the twentieth century, the adult brain was widely regarded as relatively fixed: it could store new memories, but its basic structure was thought to change little after childhood. Testing that assumption in humans is difficult, because researchers rarely find groups of adults who have undergone long, intensive and comparable training in a single skill. London’s taxi drivers proved to be an exception. If structure could change, then learning would be not only a matter of storing information but also of reshaping the very organ that stores it.
在二十世紀的大部分時間裡，成人的大腦普遍被認為相對固定：它能儲存新的記憶，但基本結構在童年之後被認為變化不大。要在人類身上檢驗這個假設很困難，因為研究者很少能找到一群接受過長期、密集、且彼此可比較之單一技能訓練的成年人。倫敦的計程車司機正是一個例外。如果結構能夠改變，那麼學習就不只是儲存資訊，而是重塑那個負責儲存的器官本身。

To be licensed, they must master The Knowledge, an exhaustive mental map of the city that typically takes years of study. In a study published in 2000, Eleanor Maguire and colleagues used structural MRI to compare the brains of 16 licensed taxi drivers — whose training had taken about two years on average — with those of men who did not drive taxis. Their attention fell on the hippocampus, a structure long associated with spatial memory. The drivers had been licensed for anywhere between a year and a half and several decades, which gave the researchers a natural range of experience to work with.
要取得執照，他們必須精通「The Knowledge」——一份涵蓋整座城市、詳盡無遺的心智地圖，通常需要多年的學習。在 2000 年發表的研究中，艾莉諾．馬奎爾與同事用結構性核磁共振，把 16 位持照計程車司機（平均訓練約兩年）的大腦，與不開計程車的男性比較。他們的焦點落在海馬迴——一個長期被認為與空間記憶有關的結構。這些司機的持照時間從一年半到數十年不等，讓研究者有一段自然的經驗範圍可以分析。

The results pointed to a redistribution rather than a simple enlargement. The posterior hippocampus was significantly larger in the drivers, whereas a more anterior region was larger in the control group. Crucially, the volume of the right posterior hippocampus correlated positively with time spent as a taxi driver, and the anterior volume correlated negatively. The authors therefore argued that the changes were acquired, reflecting what they called local plasticity in the structure of the healthy adult brain. This pattern matters because it is harder to explain by pre-existing differences alone: if people simply chose the job because of their brains, there would be little reason for the difference to grow with every additional year of driving.

結果指向的是一種重新分配，而不是單純的變大。司機的海馬迴後側明顯較大，而較前側的區域則是對照組較大。關鍵在於，右側海馬迴後側的體積與擔任計程車司機的時間呈正相關，前側體積則呈負相關。因此，作者主張這些變化是後天獲得的，反映了他們所稱的「健康成人大腦結構的局部可塑性」。這個模式很重要，因為單靠「本來就有的差異」很難解釋：如果人們只是因為大腦本來如此才選擇這份工作，那麼差異就沒有理由隨著每多開一年車而增加。

Like any single study, this one has limits. The sample was small and consisted only of men, and a correlation with experience, while suggestive, is not the same as watching the brain change over time. Nevertheless, the finding helped shift scientific opinion towards the view that sustained mental effort can leave physical traces in the adult brain — and that the brain allocates resources according to the demands we place on it.
和任何單一研究一樣，這項研究也有限制。樣本很小、只有男性，而與經驗之間的相關性雖然具有啟發性，卻不等同於親眼看見大腦隨時間改變。儘管如此，這項發現仍推動科學界的看法轉向：持續的心智努力，可以在成人大腦中留下實體痕跡——而大腦會依照我們對它的要求來分配資源。

That idea acquires new relevance in an age of satellite navigation. If spatial skill is, in part, built by the act of navigating, then handing that task to a device may reshape not only how we travel but how we think. The question is still under investigation, and convenience is not a vice. Yet the taxi drivers offer a reminder worth keeping: abilities we stop practising may not disappear overnight, but they are unlikely to grow on their own. Perhaps the most useful lesson is not to abandon technology, but to choose, now and then, to do the work ourselves.
在衛星導航的時代，這個想法有了新的意義。如果空間能力有一部分是由「自己導航」這個行為建立的，那麼把這項任務交給裝置，改變的可能不只是我們移動的方式，還有我們思考的方式。這個問題仍在研究中，而便利本身也不是一種罪過。然而，這些計程車司機提供了一個值得記住的提醒：我們不再練習的能力，也許不會一夜消失，但它們也不太可能自己長大。也許最有用的啟示不是放棄科技，而是偶爾選擇自己動手去做。

beginner.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How drivers can pass The Knowledge test in London.
Why phone maps are better than finding our own way.
How learning London’s streets may have changed taxi drivers’ brains.
Why London’s streets are small, crooked and confusing.
beginner.evidence: The back part of the hippocampus was larger in the taxi drivers.
beginner.why: 第二到四段：研究學習倫敦街道是否改變了司機的大腦。
traps: 以偏概全：考試只是第一段的背景。
捏造：作者反而建議偶爾放下手機。
以偏概全：只是第一段的背景。

beginner.q: What does “plasticity” mean in the fourth paragraph?
options: The brain’s ability to change as we use it.
The plastic that is used to make phone cases.
The size of the brain when we are born.
The skill of finding the best route in a city.
beginner.evidence: This suggests that the brain may change as we use it.
beginner.why: 前一句定義：大腦會隨著使用而改變，科學家稱之為 plasticity。
traps: 一字多義：plastic 是塑膠，但 plasticity 在這裡指可塑性。
正反顛倒：重點是「後天」改變。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：找路是司機的技能，不是這個字的意思。

beginner.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: The front part of the hippocampus was larger in the taxi drivers.
Every driver in the study took exactly two years to train.
The scientists studied the brains of 60 London taxi drivers.
The study compared taxi drivers with men who did not drive taxis.
beginner.evidence: They compared them with men who did not drive taxis.
beginner.why: 第三段：把計程車司機和不開計程車的男性做比較。
traps: 張冠李戴：較大的是海馬迴的後段（back part）。
數字錯位：兩年是平均，有人不到一年，有人三年半。
數字錯位：原文是 16 位司機。

beginner.q: Why does the writer mention phone maps in the last paragraph?
options: To prove that phone maps damage our brains.
To suggest that relying on phones may affect our own sense of direction.
To tell readers to stop using their phones completely.
To show how taxi drivers prepare for The Knowledge.
beginner.evidence: if we never find our way by ourselves, what happens to the map inside our heads?
beginner.why: 最後一段：如果從不自己找路，我們腦中的地圖會怎樣？
traps: 過度推論：原文 Scientists are still studying that question。
正反顛倒：原文說 sometimes 放下手機，不是完全不用。
張冠李戴：司機要背街道，不能用地圖。

intermediate.q: Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?
options: Intensive learning may change the structure of the adult brain.
The Knowledge is one of the most demanding tests in the world.
People with larger brains are more likely to become taxi drivers.
Phone apps have made London’s taxi drivers less skilled.
intermediate.evidence: whether this kind of intensive learning could change the physical structure of the adult brain
intermediate.why: 第二段點出研究問題，第五段說明意義：成人大腦比以前以為的更能改變。
traps: 以偏概全：只是第一段的背景。
正反顛倒：第四段的分析支持差異來自經驗，不是天生。
捏造：文中只提出問題，沒有這個結論。

intermediate.q: What does the word “posterior” in the third paragraph mean?
options: Front.
Larger.
Rear.
Right.
intermediate.evidence: the posterior, or rear, part of the hippocampus
intermediate.why: 同位語 or rear 直接解釋了 posterior。
traps: 正反顛倒：前段較大的是對照組。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：後段「比較大」，但 posterior 不是大的意思。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：第四段的 right posterior hippocampus 是「右側後段」，right 是另一個字。

intermediate.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: All the drivers had been licensed for less than a year.
A front region of the hippocampus was larger in the comparison group.
The taxi drivers simply had more brain tissue overall.
The drivers had spent about ten years training for The Knowledge.
intermediate.evidence: while a front region was larger in the comparison group
intermediate.why: 第三段：後段在司機較大，前段在對照組較大。
traps: 正反顛倒：都已取得執照超過一年半。
正反顛倒：原文 a different distribution of tissue, not simply more of it。
數字錯位：平均約兩年。

intermediate.q: Why did the team look at how long each person had worked as a driver?
options: To decide which drivers should keep their licence.
To prove that older drivers are safer on the road.
To show that phone apps had changed the drivers’ brains.
To find out whether the brain difference came from experience rather than birth.
intermediate.evidence: This suggested that the difference was acquired through experience rather than present from birth.
intermediate.why: 第四段：為了回應「是不是大腦本來就比較大的人才去當司機」這個質疑。
traps: 捏造：研究沒有涉及執照。
捏造：文中沒討論駕駛安全。
時序錯置：手機 app 是第五段提出的新問題。

advanced.q: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To argue that satellite navigation should be banned.
To describe a study suggesting that adult brains can be reshaped by experience.
To explain how taxi drivers memorise London’s streets.
To prove that the adult brain cannot change after childhood.
advanced.evidence: the finding helped shift scientific opinion towards the view that sustained mental effort can leave physical traces in the adult brain
advanced.why: 全文：用計程車司機研究挑戰「成人大腦固定不變」的舊觀念。
traps: 正反顛倒：原文 convenience is not a vice。
以偏概全：只是第二段的背景。
正反顛倒：這正是被研究挑戰的舊觀念。

advanced.q: Which of the following is closest in meaning to “redistribution” as used in the third paragraph?
options: A simple increase in the size of every brain region.
A decrease in the size of the whole brain.
A transfer of memories from one person to another.
A change in where the brain tissue was located.
advanced.evidence: The results pointed to a redistribution rather than a simple enlargement.
advanced.why: 後段變大、前段變小，是組織「重新分配」，不是整體變大。
traps: 正反顛倒：原文 rather than a simple enlargement。
捏造：文中沒說整個大腦變小。
字面誤讀：distribution 不是在人與人之間轉移。

advanced.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: The sample in the study included both men and women.
The anterior volume became larger with more years of driving.
The right posterior hippocampus was larger in drivers with more years on the job.
The study watched the drivers’ brains change over many years.
advanced.evidence: the volume of the right posterior hippocampus correlated positively with time spent as a taxi driver
advanced.why: 第三段：右側後段海馬迴的體積和開計程車的年資呈正相關。
traps: 正反顛倒：原文 consisted only of men。
正反顛倒：前段體積和年資呈負相關。
正反顛倒：第四段說相關性 is not the same as watching the brain change over time。

advanced.q: Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?
options: A difference that grows with experience is hard to explain by birth alone.
Taxi drivers are born with a larger hippocampus than other people.
Using satellite navigation has been proved to shrink the brain.
A correlation is as strong as watching the brain change over time.
advanced.evidence: there would be little reason for the difference to grow with every additional year of driving
advanced.why: 第三段：如果只是天生大腦適合才去當司機，差異就不會隨年資增加。
traps: 正反顛倒：作者認為變化是後天獲得的。
過度推論：原文 The question is still under investigation。
正反顛倒：第四段說相關性 is not the same as watching the brain change。

paras: To earn a licence to drive one of London’s famous black cabs, drivers must pass The Knowledge, a test that requires them to memorise the layout of a huge and irregular city and plan routes entirely from memory. For much of the twentieth century, the adult brain was widely believed to change little after childhood. London’s taxi drivers, who spend years in intensive training for a single skill, offered scientists a rare chance to test that belief.
想取得駕駛倫敦著名黑色計程車的執照，司機必須通過「知識大考」：記住這座龐大又不規則的城市的街道配置，並完全憑記憶規劃路線。二十世紀大部分時間裡，人們普遍認為成人的大腦在童年之後就很少改變。倫敦計程車司機為了單一技能接受多年的密集訓練，正好給科學家一個難得的機會來檢驗這個看法。

In a study published in 2000, the neuroscientist Eleanor Maguire and her colleagues used brain scans to compare 16 licensed London taxi drivers with men who did not drive taxis. The drivers had spent about two years, on average, training for The Knowledge, and some had been driving for decades. All of them had been licensed for more than a year and a half. The researchers focused on the hippocampus, a region long associated with spatial memory (our memory for places and routes).
在 2000 年發表的研究中，神經科學家艾莉諾．馬奎爾和同事用腦部掃描，比較 16 位領有執照的倫敦計程車司機和不開計程車的男性。這些司機平均花了約兩年準備知識大考，有些人已經開了幾十年車；所有人都已取得執照超過一年半。研究者聚焦在海馬迴——這個腦區長久以來被認為和空間記憶（我們對地點與路線的記憶）有關。

What they found was not a simple enlargement but a redistribution. The rear, or posterior, part of the hippocampus was significantly larger in the drivers, whereas a front region was larger in the comparison group. In other words, the drivers’ brains showed a different distribution of tissue, not simply more of it. Moreover, the longer someone had worked as a taxi driver, the larger the right posterior hippocampus tended to be. If people had simply chosen the job because of the brains they were born with, there would be little reason for the difference to grow with every year of driving.
他們發現的不是單純的變大，而是重新分配。海馬迴的後段在司機身上明顯較大，前段則是對照組較大。換句話說，司機大腦的組織分布不同，而不只是比較多。而且，開計程車的時間越久，右側海馬迴後段往往越大。如果人們只是因為天生的大腦才選了這份工作，這個差異就沒有理由隨著開車的年資逐年增加。

Like any single study, this one has limits. The sample was small and included only men, and a link with experience is not the same as watching the brain change over time. Even so, the finding was so striking that it helped shift scientific opinion towards the view that sustained mental effort can leave physical traces in the adult brain — a property the authors called plasticity.
就像任何單一研究，這項研究也有限制：樣本小、只有男性，而且「和經驗有關聯」並不等於親眼看到大腦隨時間改變。即便如此，這個發現驚人到幫助扭轉了科學界的看法，讓人們相信持續的心智努力能在成人大腦留下實體痕跡——作者稱之為可塑性。

Only now, in an age of phone maps, are we beginning to ask what happens when we hand the task of navigating to a device. The question is still under investigation, and convenience is not a crime. Yet the taxi drivers offer a reminder worth keeping: abilities we stop practising may not disappear overnight, but they are unlikely to grow on their own.
直到現在這個手機地圖的時代，我們才開始追問：把導航這件事交給裝置，會發生什麼事？這個問題仍在研究中，而方便也不是罪過。但計程車司機給了我們一個值得記住的提醒：不再練習的能力也許不會一夜消失，卻不太可能自己長大。
